tagline: Around Lake Cumberland to a waterfall that keeps a moonbow.
intro: The byway comes in pieces. Its southern run follows KY 90 from just below Burkesville east past Albany to the edge of Monticello, around the south end of Lake Cumberland, and takes up KY 90 again in McCreary County for the last miles to the lodge at Cumberland Falls. Other sections tie Edmonton, Columbia and Campbellsville to Russell Springs, Liberty and Danville, with a loop to Stanford.

It honors the settlers who came through the Cumberland Gap and stayed. The lake came much later, held back by Wolf Creek Dam for flood control and power, and runs 101 miles long. Monticello, on its shore, calls itself the Houseboat Capital of the World.

moments.title: Burkesville
moments.text: The last steamboat tied up at this Cumberland River port in 1929, a year after the first major road opened to Glasgow, and Wolf Creek Dam upstream finished the river trade.

moments.title: Albany
moments.text: Probably named for Albany, New York, though legend credits tavern patrons shouting "All for Benny" at the county seat vote, and the town still holds an All for Benny dinner.

moments.title: Cumberland Falls
moments.text: The river drops 68 feet here, one of the few places in the western hemisphere where a moonbow can often be seen on nights with a full moon.
